question: What is a container, in terms of what minibox actually asks the kernel for? Is it a small VM?
answer_hinglish:
Container koi VM nahi hai. VM ka apna kernel hota hai; container ek normal Linux process hai jo host ke HI kernel par chalta hai. Fark sirf itna hai ki kernel us process ko teen cheezein alag deta hai: (1) apne namespaces -- PID, UTS (hostname), mount, IPC, net -- taaki use host ke processes, hostname, mounts, shared memory aur network interfaces na dikhen; (2) ek alag root filesystem -- image ka rootfs, pivot_root ke baad wahi uska / ban jaata hai; (3) cgroup limits -- memory.max, pids.max, cpu.max, taaki woh host ke resources kha na jaaye.

minibox exactly yahi karta hai: container.py ka run() cgroup leaf banata hai, unshare(CLONE_NEWPID) karke INIT fork karta hai; INIT setup_container() mein unshare(mount, UTS, IPC, net), sethostname, lo up, mount plan aur pivot_root karta hai, phir CMD fork karke execvpe. Isliye README kehta hai: 'a normal process with its own namespaces, a different root filesystem, and cgroup limits'.

Important honesty point: minibox security boundary NAHI hai. User namespace nahi hai (container ka root host ka root hai, test_user_namespace_is_shared_with_the_host yeh check karta hai), capabilities drop nahi hoti, seccomp nahi hai. Toh yeh 'honest programs ko ek doosre se alag rakhna' hai, hostile code ke khilaaf protection nahi. Interview line: container = process + namespaces + root fs + cgroups, aur hardening alag layer hai.
why_needed: Docker ko black box ki tarah use karna aasaan hai, lekin debugging (PID 1 SIGTERM ignore karta hai, zombies, OOM 137) tab hi samajh aati hai jab pata ho container underneath sirf ek process hai.
real_world_analogy: Ek bade office mein cubicle: building (kernel), bijli, lift sab shared hai, lekin har team ko apni deewarein (namespaces), apna naam-plate (hostname), apni almari (root fs) aur bijli ka meter-limit (cgroup) milta hai. Alag building (VM) nahi hai.
how_it_works: Host process -> cgroup leaf create + limits write -> unshare(CLONE_NEWPID) -> fork INIT (PID 1) -> INIT: unshare(NEWNS|NEWUTS|NEWIPC|NEWNET), sethostname, lo up, apply_plan, pivot_root -> fork CMD (PID 2) -> execvpe(command, clean env). Kernel wahi hai, sirf 'view' aur 'limits' alag.
in_this_project: minibox/container.py (run, setup_container, init_main), minibox/mounts.py (build_plan, enter_root), minibox/cgroups.py (Limits, Cgroup). README ka pehla section 'it is NOT a security boundary' clearly batata hai kya nahi kiya.

def setup_container(cfg: Config, plan: mounts.Plan) -> None:

    os.unshare(os.CLONE_NEWNS | os.CLONE_NEWUTS | os.CLONE_NEWIPC | os.CLONE_NEWNET)
    socket.sethostname(cfg.hostname)
    bring_up_loopback()
    mounts.apply_plan(plan)
    mounts.enter_root(plan.new_root, use_pivot_root=cfg.use_pivot_root)

question: Which namespaces does minibox create, what does each one isolate, and how is that proven?
answer_hinglish:
minibox paanch namespaces banata hai, do jagah se. Host process unshare(CLONE_NEWPID) karta hai (uske baad ka child INIT naye PID ns mein PID 1 hota hai). Phir INIT setup_container() mein ek call mein baaki chaar: CLONE_NEWNS | CLONE_NEWUTS | CLONE_NEWIPC | CLONE_NEWNET.

- PID: container ke processes apni numbering dekhte hain; INIT PID 1, command PID 2. Fresh /proc ke saath ps sirf container ke processes dikhata hai.
- UTS: hostname alag. sethostname('box1') host ka naam nahi badalta (test_hostname_is_private).
- mount (NEWNS): mounts ki apni list; container sirf /, /dev, /dev/pts, /dev/shm, /proc dekhta hai (test_only_the_containers_own_mounts_are_visible).
- IPC: System V shared memory alag; host par shmget kiya segment container ki /proc/sysvipc/shm mein nahi dikhta (test_ipc_namespace_hides_host_shared_memory, mutation M10 ne 2 tests red kiye).
- net: naya, khaali network namespace -- sirf lo, jo minibox ioctl se up karta hai (test_only_loopback_network_and_it_is_up: lo + PING-OK).

test_every_namespace_differs_from_the_host parametrized hai pid/uts/ipc/mnt/net par: andar readlink /proc/self/ns/<ns> host ki value se alag hona chahiye. Jo NAHI hai: user namespace (test confirm karta hai woh host jaisa hai, uid 0), aur cgroup namespace -- dono README ki NOT-done list mein hain.
why_needed: Har namespace ek specific global resource ko private banata hai. Interview mein 'container = namespaces' bolna kaafi nahi; kaunsa namespace kya chhupata hai woh batana padta hai.
real_world_analogy: Hotel ke kamre: alag room number system (PID), apna door-name plate (UTS), apni almari ki list (mount), apna notice board (IPC), apna intercom jo sirf kamre ke andar baat karta hai (net with only lo).
how_it_works: unshare(flags) caller ko naye namespaces mein daal deta hai (PID ke alawa, jo next child par lagta hai). /proc/self/ns/<type> symlink 'type:[inode]' dikhata hai; alag inode = alag namespace.
in_this_project: minibox/container.py run() mein os.unshare(os.CLONE_NEWPID), setup_container() mein baaki chaar. Proof tests/integration/test_isolation.py mein: test_every_namespace_differs_from_the_host, test_hostname_is_private, test_ipc_namespace_hides_host_shared_memory, test_only_loopback_network_and_it_is_up.

# real, tests/integration/test_isolation.py
@pytest.mark.parametrize("ns", ["pid", "uts", "ipc", "mnt", "net"])
def test_every_namespace_differs_from_the_host(box, ns):
    r = box.run(f"readlink /proc/self/ns/{ns}")
    assert r.returncode == 0, r.stderr
    inside = r.stdout.strip()
    assert inside.startswith(f"{ns}:[") and inside != os.readlink(f"/proc/self/ns/{ns}")

Network sirf loopback: bahar se baat nahi (stage 4 nahi kiya)

question: Why does unshare(CLONE_NEWPID) not move the calling process into the new PID namespace, and how does that shape minibox's process design?
answer_hinglish:
Baaki namespaces (mount, UTS, IPC, net) mein unshare() caller ko turant naye namespace mein daal deta hai. PID namespace alag hai: ek process ka PID uski poori life fixed rehta hai -- getpid() ka answer beech mein badal nahi sakta, warna parent ka waitpid, signals, sab toot jayenge. Isliye kernel unshare(CLONE_NEWPID) ke baad caller ko purane namespace mein hi rehne deta hai aur sirf uske AGLE child ko naye namespace mein banata hai, aur woh pehla child wahan PID 1 hota hai.

minibox ka design isi rule se nikla: host process (run()) os.unshare(os.CLONE_NEWPID) karta hai aur turant os.fork() -- yeh child INIT hai, jo container mein PID 1 hai. INIT phir baaki namespaces unshare karta hai aur CMD fork karta hai, jo PID 2 banta hai. Agar host process khud 'container' banne ki koshish karta, toh woh host ka hi PID rakhta aur /proc mein sab host processes dikhte.

Proof: test_command_is_pid_2_and_init_is_pid_1 -- echo $$ ka output '2' aur /proc/1/cmdline mein 'minibox'. container.py ka module docstring bhi likhta hai: 'only its NEXT child is created in the new PID namespace, and that child is PID 1 there. That is why INIT is a separate process.' Ek side effect: host process khud naye PID ns ka member nahi hai, isliye woh INIT ko host-side pid se signal aur waitpid kar sakta hai.
why_needed: Yeh samjhe bina log unshare ke baad seedha exec kar dete hain aur hairaan hote hain ki ps abhi bhi host ke processes dikhata hai ya PID 1 nahi mila.
real_world_analogy: Naya mohalla (PID namespace) ban gaya, lekin purane ghar waale ka address nahi badal sakta; sirf jo bachcha ab paida hoga woh naye mohalle ka pehla resident (house no. 1) hoga.
how_it_works: unshare(CLONE_NEWPID) task ke 'pid_ns_for_children' ko set karta hai, current pid ko nahi. fork() ke waqt kernel child ko us naye ns mein allocate karta hai; pehla process ns ka init (PID 1) hota hai.
in_this_project: minibox/container.py run(): ready pipe banane ke baad os.unshare(os.CLONE_NEWPID); init_pid = os.fork(). init_main() phir cmd_pid = os.fork(). Test: tests/integration/test_isolation.py::test_command_is_pid_2_and_init_is_pid_1.

question: Walk through minibox's three-process design (host -> INIT PID 1 -> CMD PID 2). Why not simply exec the user's command as PID 1?
answer_hinglish:
Teen processes hain aur har ek ka kaam alag hai.

1) Host (minibox process): state dir + overlay dirs aur cgroup leaf banata hai, unshare(CLONE_NEWPID), INIT fork karta hai, INIT ka pid cgroup.procs mein likhta hai, phir pipe par ek byte likh kar INIT ko aage jaane deta hai. Uske baad TERM/INT/HUP/QUIT/USR1/USR2 ko INIT ko forward karta hai, waitpid(init_pid) karta hai, aur finally mein cleanup(): cgroup.kill, stats, rmdir cgroup, state dir delete.

2) INIT (PID 1, minibox ka apna Python code): unshare(mount, UTS, IPC, net), hostname, lo up, mount plan, pivot_root, phir CMD fork; uske baad sirf do duties -- waitpid(-1) loop se har orphan reap karna aur signals CMD ko forward karna. CMD exit -> INIT usi code se exit -> kernel namespace ke baaki sab ko SIGKILL karta hai.

3) CMD (PID 2): signal dispositions reset (SIGPIPE samet), chdir(workdir), execvpe(command, clean env).

Command ko seedha PID 1 kyun nahi banaya? PLAN.md: PID 1 ko kernel default signal actions nahi deta -- jis signal ka handler nahi, woh drop. Toh shell ya web server PID 1 par docker stop ka SIGTERM chupchaap ignore karta hai, aur orphans ko reap nahi karta toh zombies jama hote hain. Yeh dono kaam ek chhota trusted init karta hai -- wahi jo docker run --init / tini add karta hai. Proof: test_sigterm_stops_a_command_without_a_handler -- exec sleep 1000 PID 2 par hai, SIGTERM par 143 aur 3 s ke andar. Mutations M5 (no reaping), M6 (INIT no forward), M7 (host no forward) sab pakde gaye.
why_needed: Production mein 'docker stop 10 s tak latka phir SIGKILL' aur 'zombie processes' bahut common complaints hain; dono ka root cause PID 1 semantics hai.
real_world_analogy: Building ka chowkidar (INIT): residents (CMD) apna kaam karte hain, chowkidar sirf gate par aaye notice (signals) andar pahunchata hai aur khaali flats (zombies) saaf karta hai. Society office (host) bahar se chowkidar ko hi notice deta hai.
how_it_works: host: pipe, unshare(NEWPID), fork -> add_pid -> write pipe -> signal handlers -> waitpid -> cleanup. INIT: read pipe -> setup_container -> fork CMD -> handlers -> loop waitpid(-1) until pid == cmd_pid -> return exit_code_from_status. CMD: SIG_DFL resets -> chdir -> execvpe.
in_this_project: minibox/container.py: run() (host), init_main() (INIT aur CMD dono, fork ke do branches), cleanup(). Config mein reap_zombies aur forward_signals flags hain jo sirf tests ke liye switch hote hain.
advantages: User ka command normal PID 2 semantics paata hai: default signal actions kaam karte hain
Zombie reaping guaranteed, command chahe kuch bhi ho
Container ki life = command ki life, kernel ke ns-teardown se
disadvantages: Har container mein ek extra Python process (memory + start time)
Host process SIGKILL ho jaaye toh koi cleanup nahi karta (README NOT-done list)
common_mistakes: Shell ko PID 1 bana kar maan lena SIGTERM kaam karega
INIT mein sirf waitpid(cmd_pid) karna -- orphans zombie bante hain (M5)
Host side forward bhool jaana -- INIT tak signal hi nahi pahunchta (M7)
follow_up_questions: INIT ko Python ki jagah C/Go mein likhna kab worth hai?
exec into a running container (docker exec) is design mein kaise fit hoga?
Agar CMD khud ek init ho (systemd), tab kya karoge?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Extra INIT process ki cost (ek Python interpreter, start time ka hissa) ke badle har command ko sahi PID 1 behaviour milta hai bina command badle. Alternative 'command as PID 1' sasta hai lekin har image ko khud signal handling aur reaping karni padti.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Host process SIGKILL -> koi forward/cleanup nahi; container chalta rehta hai, cgroup aur state dir bachte hain. INIT crash -> kernel namespace kill karta hai, host 125 ya 128+N dekhta hai. M6 mutation run mein INIT ne SIGTERM forward nahi kiya toh do containers chalte reh gaye aur unhe cgroup.kill se roka gaya (SERVER_RUN.md).
advanced.alternatives: Command ko hi PID 1 banana; tini/dumb-init jaisa chhota C init exec karna; PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER se host process ko subreaper banana (lekin PID ns ka init phir bhi chahiye).
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 10x-100x containers par har container ka Python INIT memory aur start time mein dikhega; INIT ko chhote static binary se replace karna logical step hai. Yeh measure nahi kiya, sirf 1 container ka start (18 ms inner) measured hai.
advanced.production_improvements: Chhota native init, host-side supervisor jo crash ke baad leftovers saaf kare (abhi minibox gc nahi hai), stop timeout ke baad SIGKILL escalation, aur INIT ka exit reason stats mein.

question: Why does PID 1 inside a PID namespace ignore SIGTERM by default, and how does minibox make docker-stop-style SIGTERM work?
answer_hinglish:
Kernel PID namespace ke init (PID 1) ko protect karta hai: us par koi signal tabhi deliver hota hai jab PID 1 ne us signal ka handler install kiya ho. Default action (jaise SIGTERM ka 'terminate') PID 1 par apply nahi hota -- signal bas drop ho jaata hai. Exception: SIGKILL aur SIGSTOP agar ANCESTOR namespace se bheje gaye hon. Wajah: init mar gaya toh poora namespace mar jaata hai, toh galti se kill na ho.

Iska matlab: agar user ka shell ya server PID 1 hota, toh docker stop ka SIGTERM kuch nahi karta (aur docker grace period ke baad SIGKILL karta).

minibox mein chain do hops ki hai. Host process run() mein FORWARDED_SIGNALS (TERM, INT, HUP, QUIT, USR1, USR2) ke liye handler lagata hai jo os.kill(init_pid, sig) karta hai. INIT init_main() mein unhi signals ke handlers lagata hai jo os.kill(cmd_pid, sig) karte hain -- handler hai, isliye kernel deliver karta hai. CMD (PID 2) exec se pehle sab ko SIG_DFL karta hai, toh wahan normal default action chalta hai.

Tests: test_sigterm_is_forwarded_to_the_command (trap wala shell 'got-term' print karke 42 se exit), test_sigterm_stops_a_command_without_a_handler (exec sleep 1000 -> 143, 3 s ke andar). Mutation M6 (INIT forward nahi karta): 2 failed + 2 errors; M7 (host forward nahi karta): 2 + 3 errors. M6 ke pehle run mein do containers chalte reh gaye the aur cgroup.kill se roke gaye.
why_needed: Graceful shutdown (connections drain, files flush) SIGTERM par depend karta hai. PID 1 par yeh silently fail hota hai, aur symptom sirf 'stop slow hai' dikhta hai.
real_world_analogy: Raja (PID 1) ke paas sirf woh chitthi pahunchti hai jiske liye usne munshi (handler) rakha hai; baaki chitthiyan darbaan hi phenk deta hai. minibox ka INIT munshi rakhta hai jo chitthi aage CMD ko de deta hai.
how_it_works: Kernel signal delivery mein check: target ns init hai aur handler SIG_DFL hai aur sender same ns ya signal SIGKILL/SIGSTOP from ancestor nahi -> ignore. INIT Python signal.signal(sig, forward) se handler install karta hai, toh check pass.

advantages: User ke command ko normal signal semantics milte hain
Dono hops alag mutations se prove kiye (M6, M7)
disadvantages: Sirf listed 6 signals forward hote hain (SIGWINCH jaise nahi)
Handlers fork ke baad install hote hain; CMD fork aur handler ke beech chhota window hai jismein aaya SIGTERM INIT par drop ho sakta hai
common_mistakes: Sochna ki 'kill -TERM 1' andar se bhi kaam karega bina handler ke
Sirf INIT mein forward karna, host mein nahi -- tab signal INIT tak pahunchta hi nahi (M7)
CMD mein inherited handlers/ignores reset na karna

Forwarding window (fork ke baad, handler se pehle) ko kaise band karoge?
Process group ko signal forward karna vs sirf CMD ko -- fark?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Do-hop forwarding simple hai aur user command ko kuch nahi badalna padta. Cost: har signal do baar handle hota hai aur list hard-coded hai.
advanced.failure_scenarios: M6 run mein INIT ne forward nahi kiya -> test ka container kabhi nahi ruka, aur agle mutation runs ne uske cgroups dekhe; fix: fixture ab leftover cgroups ko kill karke fail karta hai. Handler install hone se pehle aaya signal drop ho sakta hai (code mein dikhta hai, test nahi kiya).
advanced.alternatives: Command ko PID 1 banana aur use handler likhne ko kehna; tini jaisa init jo process group ko forward kare; signalfd/sigprocmask se signals block karke fork se pehle hi pending rakhna.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Signals per-container hain, toh container count badhne se design nahi badalta. Zyada containers par ek supervisor (host process per container ke bajaye) ko signal routing table chahiye hogi -- yeh minibox mein nahi hai.
advanced.production_improvements: Fork se pehle signals block karna aur handler ke baad unblock (window band), SIGWINCH/SIGCONT forward, stop ke liye timeout + SIGKILL escalation, aur forward hue signals ka log.

question: How does minibox's INIT reap zombies, and why must it call waitpid(-1) instead of waitpid(cmd_pid)?
answer_hinglish:
Jab koi process exit hota hai toh kernel uski process-table entry tab tak rakhta hai jab tak parent wait() karke exit status na le le -- tab tak woh 'zombie' hai. Agar parent pehle mar gaya, toh child orphan ho jaata hai aur kernel use namespace ke PID 1 ko re-parent kar deta hai. Matlab container ke andar jitne bhi orphans bane, sab INIT ke children ban jaate hain, aur unka wait karna INIT ki zimmedari hai.

init_main() ka loop: os.waitpid(-1, 0) -- '-1' matlab koi bhi child. Har baar ek child reap hota hai; agar woh cmd_pid hai toh exit_code_from_status(status) return, warna loop chalta rehta hai (woh ek orphan tha, ab saaf). ChildProcessError aaye (koi child bacha hi nahi) toh EXIT_SETUP_FAILED.

waitpid(cmd_pid) kyun galat: tab INIT sirf command ka intezaar karta, aur beech mein re-parent hue orphans exit hone ke baad zombie bane rehte, namespace khatam hone tak. Long-running server jo har request par child fork karta hai, process table bhar sakta hai -- aur pids.max = 32 jaise limit mein zombies bhi count hote hain.

Test test_orphans_are_reaped_by_init: andar ek inner sh 'sleep 0.2 &' chhod kar exit karta hai, sleep INIT ko re-parent hota hai; 1.2 s baad saare /proc/*/status mein 'zombie' nahi hona chahiye. Mutation M5 (INIT sirf command ka wait kare, reap_zombies=False path) ne yeh test red kiya.
why_needed: Zombie leak dheere dheere hota hai aur pids limit ya process table ko bhar deta hai; root cause samajhna production debugging ka basic hai.
real_world_analogy: Hostel warden (PID 1): jin bachchon ke parents chale gaye, unka checkout form (exit status) warden ko hi sign karna padta hai, warna room (process table entry) kabhi khaali nahi hota.
how_it_works: child exit -> state Z -> parent waitpid -> entry freed. Parent pehle mara -> child reparent to ns init. INIT: loop waitpid(-1, 0) -> pid == cmd_pid ? return code : continue.
in_this_project: minibox/container.py init_main() ka while True loop; Config.reap_zombies (sirf test/mutation ke liye False). Test tests/integration/test_isolation.py::test_orphans_are_reaped_by_init.

# real, tests/integration/test_isolation.py
def test_orphans_are_reaped_by_init(box):
    # the inner sh exits at once, its 'sleep 0.2' is re-parented to PID 1 and exits 0.2 s later;
    # 1 s after that it must be gone, not a zombie
    r = box.run("sh -c 'sleep 0.2 &'; sleep 1.2; grep -h '^State' /proc/[0-9]*/status | sort | uniq -c")

    assert "zombie" not in r.stdout, r.stdout

question: What exit codes does minibox return (0-255, 125, 126, 127, 128+N), and what does each mean?
answer_hinglish:
minibox docker jaise exit codes deta hai taaki scripts aur CI unhe same tarah samajh sakein:

- Command ka apna code: exit 0 -> 0, exit 7 -> 7, exit 255 -> 255.
- 128+N: command signal N se mara. kill -9 -> 137 (128+9), kill -TERM -> 143 (128+15). OOM killer bhi SIGKILL bhejta hai, isliye memory limit hit hone par 137 aata hai -- README ka L2 table: 3 of 3 hogs exit 137, oom_kill 1, peak 64.0 MiB.
- 125: minibox khud container set up nahi kar paaya -- rootfs directory nahi hai, name already use mein hai, cgroup controller missing, mount fail, workdir nahi mila, ya run() ka koi OSError/RuntimeError/ValueError.
- 126: command mila lekin execute nahi ho sakta (PermissionError) -- test /etc/passwd chalata hai.
- 127: command nahi mila (FileNotFoundError) -- test /no/such/binary chalata hai aur stderr mein 'not found' check karta hai.

Constants container.py mein hain: EXIT_SETUP_FAILED = 125, EXIT_NOT_EXECUTABLE = 126, EXIT_NOT_FOUND = 127. 126/127 CMD ke andar execvpe ke exceptions se aate hain aur os._exit se nikalte hain; INIT us status ko exit_code_from_status se convert karta hai aur khud usi code se exit karta hai; host process INIT ka status phir se convert karta hai. question: Explain exit_code_from_status. How is a raw waitpid status encoded, and how does minibox turn death-by-signal into 128+N?
answer_hinglish:
os.waitpid jo status deta hai woh ek packed integer hai. POSIX encoding: normal exit mein exit code high byte mein hota hai (status = code << 8), aur signal se mara toh low 7 bits mein signal number hota hai (core dump flag ek bit upar). Isliye unit test raw values use karta hai: exit_code_from_status(7 << 8) == 7, (0) == 0, (9) == 137, (15) == 143.

minibox khud bits nahi kholta. Python 3.9+ ka os.waitstatus_to_exitcode(status) yeh decode karta hai: normal exit par positive code, signal par NEGATIVE signal number (SIGKILL -> -9). Function bas itna karta hai: code < 0 ho toh 128 - code (128 - (-9) = 137), warna code jaisa hai. Do lines, koi WIFEXITED/WTERMSIG manual masking nahi.

Yeh function do jagah chalta hai: INIT mein (CMD ka status -> INIT ka exit code) aur host mein (INIT ka status -> minibox ka exit code). Kyunki INIT normal exit karta hai os._exit(code) se, host ko 137 bhi 'normal exit 137' ki tarah milta hai, toh double conversion safe hai. Agar INIT khud kisi signal se mare (jaise cgroup OOM ne INIT ko hi maara), host ko signal status milta hai aur wahi 128+N mapping lagti hai.

Mutation M11 (death by signal 128+N par map nahi kiya) ne integration mein 3 tests red kiye -- test_exit_code_is_propagated ke 137 aur 143 cases aur test_sigterm_stops_a_command_without_a_handler.
why_needed: Bina mapping ke signal death ka code galat aata (Python negative deta hai, aur sys.exit negative ko 0-255 mein wrap kar deta), aur caller OOM ko pehchaan nahi pata.
real_world_analogy: Hospital report ka code: 'discharged with note X' (exit code) vs 'emergency type N' (signal). Report card par emergency ko 128+N likhne ki convention hai taaki dono ek hi column mein fit hon.
how_it_works: raw status -> os.waitstatus_to_exitcode -> >=0: exit code; <0: -signum -> 128 + signum. INIT: return exit_code_from_status(status) -> os._exit(code). Host: phir waitpid -> same function.

question: What is the difference between chroot and pivot_root, and why does minibox use pivot_root?
answer_hinglish:
chroot(dir) sirf ek cheez badalta hai: IS process ke path lookups kahan se shuru hon. Host ka poora filesystem tree namespace mein ab bhi mounted hai; process ka '/' bas ek pointer badal gaya. Root process (CAP_SYS_CHROOT ke saath, jo minibox container rakhta hai) usse wapas bahar nikal sakta hai -- classic chroot escape.

pivot_root(new_root, put_old) poore mount namespace ka root MOUNT swap karta hai: new_root namespace ka / ban jaata hai aur purana root put_old par chala jaata hai. Phir minibox umount2('/.oldroot', MNT_DETACH) se purana root detach karta hai aur directory rmdir. Ab namespace mein host ka tree kahin mounted hi nahi hai, toh '..' se climb karne ke liye kuch bacha hi nahi.

minibox mein: mounts.enter_root(new_root, use_pivot_root=True) yeh karta hai. chroot wala branch sirf ek test ke liye exist karta hai jo fark prove karta hai. Do tests: test_pivot_root_cannot_be_escaped (escape fail) aur test_chroot_alone_can_be_escaped (control: wahi escape chroot par host-only marker file tak pahunch jaata hai). Mutation M1 (pivot_root ki jagah chroot) ne pehla test red kiya. Saath hi README ka caveat: pivot_root sirf YEH raasta band karta hai; sab capabilities rakhne wala root abhi bhi doosre tareekon se (mknod + mount host disk) bahar ja sakta hai.
why_needed: Bahut tutorials chroot se 'container' banate hain; interview mein yeh pehchaanna ki chroot isolation nahi hai, basic expectation hai.
real_world_analogy: chroot = kisi ko ek kamre mein bitha kar kehna 'yahi tumhari duniya hai', jabki darwaza khula hai. pivot_root + detach = poori building hi badal di aur purani building ka raasta tod diya.
how_it_works: chroot: current->fs->root = dir. pivot_root: namespace ka root mount -> new_root, old root mount -> put_old. umount2(MNT_DETACH): old root lazily detach, namespace se gayab.

question: Walk through the chroot escape step by step, why pivot_root stops it, and how the two tests prove it (including why the second test is a control).
answer_hinglish:
Escape (README ka pseudo-code): mkdir('x'); chroot('x'); -- naya root /x hai lekin CWD abhi bhi '/' hai, yaani naye root ke BAHAR. Phir chdir('..') 64 baar: kernel '..' ko process ke root par tabhi rokta hai jab path walk us root se GUZRE; humara cwd root ke andar hai hi nahi, toh walk chalta rehta hai aur host ke real / tak pahunch jaata hai. Phir chroot('.') -- ab host ka / hi root hai. Escaped. Yeh root process ke liye kaam karta hai jiske paas CAP_SYS_CHROOT hai, aur minibox container saari capabilities rakhta hai.

pivot_root kyun rokta hai: pivot_root namespace ka root mount badalta hai aur minibox purana root /.oldroot se MNT_DETACH karke rmdir karta hai. Ab container khud bhi chroot('/escape-dir') karke cwd bahar rakhe, toh bhi '..' climb karke jo top milta hai woh naye root mount ka top hai -- us mount ke upar namespace mein kuch mounted nahi. Host tree hi nahi hai.

Test _escape_attempt forked child mein ASLI setup_container() chalata hai (overlay ke saath), confirm karta hai marker pehle visible nahi, phir exactly yahi escape karta hai aur pipe par '1' ya '0' bhejta hai ki host-only HOST-ONLY-MARKER file dikhi ya nahi. test_pivot_root_cannot_be_escaped expect karta hai False. test_chroot_alone_can_be_escaped (use_pivot_root=False) expect karta hai True -- yeh control experiment hai: agar escape code hi toota hota (jaise marker path galat), toh pehla test bina kuch prove kiye green hota. Control dikhata hai ki yahi code chroot par sach mein bahar nikalta hai. M1 (pivot_root -> chroot) ne pehla test red kiya.

question: Explain enter_root line by line: pivot_root, chdir('/'), umount2(MNT_DETACH), rmdir. What breaks if a step is skipped?
answer_hinglish:
enter_root(new_root) ke chaar steps:

1) libc.pivot_root(new_root, new_root/.oldroot): namespace ka root mount new_root ban jaata hai, purana root .oldroot par chala jaata hai. .oldroot directory build_plan ka aakhri step (Mkdir 0o700) pehle hi bana chuka hai, kyunki put_old new_root ke andar existing directory honi chahiye.

2) os.chdir('/'): pivot_root process ka cwd khud nahi badalta. Cwd purane tree mein ho sakta hai (host path). '/' par aane se cwd naye root mein aa jaata hai -- warna cwd purane root ka reference pakde rehta aur umount bhi mushkil.

3) libc.umount2('/.oldroot', MNT_DETACH): purana root (poora host tree) namespace se detach. MNT_DETACH lazy unmount hai: busy ho tab bhi mount tree se turant hat jaata hai. Normal umount EBUSY de sakta tha kyunki uske neeche bahut submounts hain.

4) os.rmdir('/.oldroot'): khaali directory hata do taaki container mein ajeeb /.oldroot na dikhe.

Step 3 skip karo = mutation M2: host ka poora tree /.oldroot par container ke andar visible -- test_only_the_containers_own_mounts_are_visible (jo /proc/mounts mein exactly /, /dev, /dev/pts, /dev/shm, /proc expect karta hai) red. pivot_root ko chroot se replace = M1. libc.pivot_root koi glibc wrapper nahi -- syscall number se call hota hai (aarch64 41, x86_64 155), aur _check failure par errno ke saath OSError deta hai.
why_needed: pivot_root ko 'ek call' samajhna galti hai; bina detach ke host tree container mein mount ki tarah pada rehta hai aur saara isolation bekaar.
real_world_analogy: Ghar shift karna: naye ghar mein jao (pivot_root), apna saaman bhi naye ghar mein rakho (chdir), purane ghar ki chabi phenk do (detach), aur purane ghar ka khaali dabba bhi hata do (rmdir).
how_it_works: pivot_root -> ns root = new_root, old at put_old; chdir('/') -> cwd fixed; umount2(MNT_DETACH) -> old tree detached lazily; rmdir -> mountpoint dir gone.

question: Why is the mount setup built as a plan of data (build_plan returning Mount/Mkdir/Mknod/Symlink steps) and then applied, instead of calling mount() directly?

question: Why must the first mount step be mount(NULL, '/', MS_REC|MS_PRIVATE)? What happened in mutation M4, and how would you diagnose leaked mounts?
answer_hinglish:
Naya mount namespace (CLONE_NEWNS) parent ke mounts ki COPY se shuru hota hai, propagation settings ke saath. systemd hosts par '/' shared mount hota hai (SERVER_RUN.md: server par read-only check mein '/' shared mila). Shared peer group ka matlab: is namespace mein jo bhi mount neeche hoga, woh peer (host) namespace mein bhi propagate hoga. Toh bina private kiye, container ka overlay, proc, /dev tmpfs, devpts, shm sab host par bhi dikhne lagte. Doosra problem: pivot_root shared mounts ko refuse karta hai (EINVAL).

Isliye build_plan ka step 1 hamesha Mount(None, '/', None, MS_REC | MS_PRIVATE) hai -- poore tree ko recursively private, ab propagation band. Unit test test_first_step_makes_everything_private dono plans (bind aur overlay) mein yeh check karta hai.

M4 mutation (2026-11-21, 18:18): yeh step hataya gaya. Exactly prediction ke mutabik: 2 isolation tests fail + 2 errors, pivot_root ne shared mount refuse kiya, aur 10 mounts host ke /proc/mounts mein leak hue (normal 29 lines). Unhe sudo umount -R <state>/merged se haath se hatana pada; /proc/mounts wapas 29 lines, 0 h16 waale.

Diagnose kaise: (1) host par grep -c overlay /proc/mounts aur wc -l, before/after compare; (2) findmnt -o TARGET,PROPAGATION se dekho '/' shared hai ya nahi; (3) conftest ka no_leftovers fixture har test ke baad host /proc/self/mounts mein '/state/' ya 'minibox' dhoondta hai aur fail karta hai -- isi se errors count aaye.
why_needed: Mount propagation sabse confusing Linux topics mein se hai; galti ka symptom host par dikhta hai (leaked mounts, unmount na hone wale dirs), container mein nahi.

question: Why does minibox bind-mount the rootfs onto itself when --no-overlay is used? What does the overlay root step do instead?
answer_hinglish:
pivot_root(new_root, put_old) ki ek precondition hai: new_root ek MOUNT POINT hona chahiye, sirf directory nahi. Image ka rootfs (jaise ~/images/alpine/rootfs) host filesystem ki ek normal directory hai. Isliye --no-overlay mode mein build_plan step 2 Mount(rootfs, rootfs, None, MS_BIND | MS_REC) add karta hai -- directory ko khud par bind mount, ab woh mount point hai aur pivot_root accept karta hai. MS_REC isliye ki rootfs ke neeche koi submounts hon toh woh bhi aayein.

Default (overlay) mode mein yeh zaroorat overlay khud poori karta hai: Mount('overlay', merged, 'overlay', 0, 'lowerdir=<rootfs>,upperdir=<state>/upper,workdir=<state>/work'). merged ek fresh mount point hai aur wahi new_root banta hai. lowerdir image hai jo kabhi likha nahi jaata; container ke saare writes upper mein jaate hain, jo cleanup() container ke baad shutil.rmtree se delete karta hai -- har run fresh image se. overlay_options ',' ya ':' wale paths refuse karta hai (overlayfs option separators) bajaye escaping ke.

question: Why does minibox mount a fresh /proc inside the container, and why with nosuid, nodev, noexec?
answer_hinglish:
/proc koi real directory nahi hai -- yeh procfs hai, ek kernel-generated filesystem jo process information dikhata hai. Important baat: procfs mount ke waqt us PID namespace se bandh jaata hai jismein mount karne wala hai. Image ki /proc ek khaali directory hai (kuch nahi dikhega), aur host ka /proc host ke saikdon processes dikhata. Isliye INIT naye PID namespace mein hote hue new_root/proc par fresh procfs mount karta hai -- ab ps, $$, /proc/1/cmdline sab container ki numbering dikhate hain.

build_plan mein: Mkdir(new_root/proc), phir Mount('proc', new_root/proc, 'proc', MS_NOSUID | MS_NOEXEC | MS_NODEV). Flags: nosuid (setuid bits ignore), noexec (wahan se binaries execute nahi), nodev (device files interpret nahi) -- /proc mein in teeno ki koi legit zaroorat nahi, toh band. Unit test test_proc_is_mounted_inside_new_root_with_safe_flags yeh exact flags check karta hai.

Mutation M3 (/proc remount nahi) ne 12 isolation tests red kiye -- kyunki bahut saare tests andar /proc padhte hain. Note: /sys mount NAHI hota aur /proc/kcore jaisi files mask nahi hoti (README NOT-done list).

real_world_analogy: Naye office mein employee directory (proc) purane office ki copy lagao toh galat log dikhenge; naye office ki live directory lagani padti hai jo sirf yahan ke log dikhaye.
how_it_works: procfs mount -> superblock tied to mounter's PID ns -> /proc/<pid> entries are pids in that ns. Mounted before pivot_root at new_root/proc, so after pivot it is /proc.

question: How does minibox build a minimal /dev (tmpfs, mknod, symlinks, devpts, shm), and why not just bind the host's /dev?
answer_hinglish:
Host ka /dev bind karna matlab container ko host ki disks (/dev/sda, /dev/vda, /dev/nvme0n1), /dev/mem sab de dena. minibox runc jaisa chhota set banata hai, build_plan ke steps se:

1) Mkdir new_root/dev, phir tmpfs mount (MS_NOSUID | MS_STRICTATIME, 'mode=755,size=65536k') -- fresh, memory-backed, image ko touch nahi karta.
2) Mknod DEVICES list se: null (1,3), zero (1,5), full (1,7), random (1,8), urandom (1,9), tty (5,0), mode 0666. apply_step pehle lexists hone par unlink, phir os.mknod(S_IFCHR, makedev(major, minor)) aur chmod (umask bypass).
3) Symlinks: fd -> /proc/self/fd, stdin/stdout/stderr -> /proc/self/fd/0,1,2, ptmx -> pts/ptmx.
4) devpts at /dev/pts with 'newinstance,ptmxmode=0666,mode=620' -- apna alag pty instance, host ke ptys nahi dikhte.
5) /dev/shm tmpfs, mode 1777 (sticky, sab likh sakein), nosuid/nodev/noexec.

Integration test_minimal_dev ls /dev ka exact set check karta hai aur /dev/null, urandom (16 bytes), zero (00 00 00 00) kaam karte hain; test_host_block_devices_are_absent. Caveat: container CAP_MKNOD rakhta hai, toh woh khud host disk ka node bana sakta hai -- yeh security boundary nahi.
why_needed: Programs /dev/null, /dev/urandom, /dev/tty assume karte hain; bina inke bahut cheezein toot ti hain, aur zyada dene se host hardware expose hota hai.
real_world_analogy: Hotel room mein sirf zaroori switches (light, fan, AC) -- building ka main electrical panel (host disks) room mein nahi lagate.

question: Coding exercise: bring up the loopback interface in a new network namespace without iproute2. Explain minibox's bring_up_loopback (ioctl, struct ifreq packing).
answer_hinglish:
Naye network namespace mein sirf 'lo' hota hai aur woh DOWN hota hai -- ping 127.0.0.1 bhi fail. Normally 'ip link set lo up' karte, lekin image mein iproute2 ho zaroori nahi, aur minibox stdlib-only hai. Isliye bring_up_loopback() seedha kernel se ioctl karta hai, jo 'ifconfig lo up' andar se karta hai.

Steps: (1) ek AF_INET SOCK_DGRAM socket kholo -- interface ioctls kisi bhi socket fd par chalte hain, koi connection nahi. (2) struct ifreq banao: 16 bytes interface name, phir union jiska pehla field short flags hai. Python mein struct.pack('16sH22x', b'lo', 0) -- 16s name (null padded), H unsigned short flags, 22x padding taaki total 40 bytes (sizeof ifreq) ho. (3) SIOCGIFFLAGS (0x8913) se current flags padho; result unpack karke [1] = flags. (4) flags | IFF_UP (0x1) karke SIOCSIFFLAGS (0x8914) se likho. Read-modify-write isliye ki baaki flags (jaise LOOPBACK) na mitein.

fcntl function ke andar import hota hai kyunki fcntl Linux-only hai aur module Windows par unit tests ke liye import hona chahiye. Yeh INIT ke setup_container mein unshare ke baad aur mounts se pehle chalta hai (CAP_NET_ADMIN chahiye, root hai). Test test_only_loopback_network_and_it_is_up: /proc/net/dev mein sirf 'lo' aur ping 127.0.0.1 -> PING-OK. Bahar ka networking (veth, bridge, NAT) stage 4 hai aur NOT done.
why_needed: Container mein bahut programs localhost par bind/connect karte hain (health checks, sidecars). lo down ho toh woh ajeeb tareeke se fail karte hain.
real_world_analogy: Naye flat mein main switch (lo) OFF milta hai; electrician (iproute2) na ho toh khud panel khol kar switch ON karna -- pehle dekho kaunse switch on hain, phir sirf main ON karo.
how_it_works: socket(AF_INET, SOCK_DGRAM) -> ioctl(SIOCGIFFLAGS, ifreq{name='lo'}) -> flags |= IFF_UP -> ioctl(SIOCSIFFLAGS, ifreq{name='lo', flags}) -> lo UP in this net ns.

# real, minibox/container.py
def bring_up_loopback() -> None:
    """ifconfig lo up, with SIOCGIFFLAGS / SIOCSIFFLAGS on a plain socket (no iproute2 needed)."""
    import fcntl  # Linux only; imported here so the module still imports on Windows for unit tests

    siocgifflags, siocsifflags, iff_up = 0x8913, 0x8914, 0x1
    with socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM) as s:
        ifreq = struct.pack("16sH22x", b"lo", 0)
        flags = struct.unpack("16sH22x", fcntl.ioctl(s.fileno(), siocgifflags, ifreq))[1]
        fcntl.ioctl(s.fileno(), siocsifflags, struct.pack("16sH22x", b"lo", flags | iff_up))

question: Inside the container, `yes | head -n 1` printed a write error instead of ending quietly. What is the cause and how does minibox fix it?
answer_hinglish:
Error identify: 'yes' ko head ke exit hone ke baad pipe par likhne par EPIPE milta hai aur woh 'write error' print karta hai. Normal shell mein aisa nahi hota kyunki wahan 'yes' SIGPIPE se chupchaap mar jaata hai (default action terminate).

Likely cause: Python startup par SIGPIPE ko SIG_IGN kar deta hai (taaki Python code ko exception mile). Aur Unix rule: exec ke baad signal HANDLERS reset ho jaate hain (kyunki handler code naye program mein exist nahi karta), lekin IGNORED dispositions exec ke paar survive karte hain. minibox Python hai, toh CMD process (fork of INIT, fork of minibox) SIGPIPE-ignored state inherit karta hai, aur exec ke baad 'yes' bhi SIGPIPE ignore karta hai -> EPIPE -> error message.

Investigate kaise: andar grep SigIgn /proc/self/status dekho -- bit 13 (SIGPIPE) set hoga. Ya same command host ke python subprocess se chalao vs shell se.

Smallest fix: CMD branch mein exec se pehle signal.signal(SIGPIPE, SIG_DFL) -- minibox yeh SIGINT (Python ka handler), SIGTTOU aur saare FORWARDED_SIGNALS ke liye bhi karta hai. Kyun kaam karta hai: exec se pehle disposition default, toh naya program normal Unix behaviour se shuru hota hai.

Test test_sigpipe_has_its_default_action_in_the_command: stdout ['y', 'done'] aur stderr exactly ''. Mutation M8 (SIGPIPE ignored chhoda) ne yeh 1 test red kiya.
why_needed: Python (ya kisi bhi runtime) se processes launch karne waale tools mein yeh classic bug hai; subprocess module ka restore_signals=True isi ke liye hai.
real_world_analogy: Purane kirayedaar ne bell ka wire kaat diya (ignore). Naya kirayedaar (exec) apna furniture laata hai (handlers reset), lekin kata hua wire (ignore) waisa hi rehta hai jab tak koi electrician (SIG_DFL) theek na kare.
how_it_works: Python start: SIGPIPE -> SIG_IGN. fork: dispositions copied. exec: handlers -> SIG_DFL, SIG_IGN stays. Fix: before execvpe, signal(SIGPIPE, SIG_DFL).

question: Why does minibox build a clean environment for the command instead of inheriting the host's, and what does container_env contain?
answer_hinglish:
Agar host ka environment container mein copy ho jaaye toh do problems: (1) secrets leak -- host par sudo chalate waqt AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, tokens, SSH agent socket jaise variables container ke command ko mil jaate; (2) reproducibility -- container ka behaviour host ke random variables (PYTHONPATH, LD_LIBRARY_PATH) par depend karne lagta.

container_env(cfg) sirf yeh deta hai: PATH = DEFAULT_PATH ('/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin'), HOME = '/root', HOSTNAME = cfg.hostname, TERM = host ka TERM ya 'xterm'. Phir har --env/-e K=V item partition('=') se split hota hai -- pehle '=' par, toh 'B=x=y' ka value 'x=y'. '=' na ho ya key khaali ho toh ValueError ('--env needs KEY=VALUE'), jo run() mein 125 ban jaata hai. User ka K=V default ko override kar sakta hai (test mein PATH=/bin).

Yeh env host process mein run() ke shuru mein banta hai aur CMD os.execvpe(command[0], command, env) ko deta hai -- execvpe isi env ke PATH se command dhoondta hai. question: When stdin is a terminal, the command takes its own process group and the terminal's foreground. Explain setpgid/tcsetpgrp/SIGTTOU here, and what is honestly not tested.
answer_hinglish:
Problem: terminal par Ctrl-C dabane se kernel SIGINT terminal ke FOREGROUND PROCESS GROUP ke har process ko bhejta hai. minibox host, INIT aur CMD normally ek hi process group mein hote (jo shell ne minibox ke liye banaya). Toh Ctrl-C teeno ko jaata -- host process aur INIT bhi signal handle karte (forward), aur command ko signal do baar ya ajeeb order mein mil sakta.

minibox ka code (init_main CMD branch, sirf jab os.isatty(0)): (1) signal.signal(SIGTTOU, SIG_IGN) -- background process group ka process agar terminal settings badle (tcsetpgrp) toh kernel use SIGTTOU bhejta hai jo default se stop kar deta; ignore karne se call chal jaati hai. (2) os.setpgid(0, 0) -- CMD apna naya process group banata hai (pgid = apna pid). (3) os.tcsetpgrp(0, os.getpgrp()) -- terminal ka foreground group CMD ka group bana do. Ab Ctrl-C sirf command tak jaata hai, jaise bina minibox ke. Phir reset loop SIGTTOU ko wapas SIG_DFL karta hai exec se pehle.

Ek subtle point: CMD naye PID namespace mein hai, lekin terminal aur process groups kernel-level objects hain; isatty(0) true hai kyunki stdin host ka terminal fd inherit hua hai -- koi pty allocate nahi hoti.

Honest part: README clearly kehta hai yeh code path likha gaya hai par TESTED NAHI hai, kyunki integration tests bina terminal ke chalte hain (subprocess pipes). Aur -t (TTY allocation), pty inside container -- NOT implemented.
why_needed: Interactive containers (docker run -it) mein Ctrl-C, job control aur terminal ownership ka galat handling sabse irritating UX bugs deta hai.
real_world_analogy: Class mein teacher (terminal) jab 'chup!' (Ctrl-C) bolti hai toh front bench (foreground group) ke sab bachche sunte hain. CMD ko alag front bench par bitha diya, aur minibox/INIT peeche chale gaye.
how_it_works: isatty(0) -> ignore SIGTTOU -> setpgid(0,0) -> tcsetpgrp(0, getpgrp()) -> reset dispositions incl. SIGTTOU -> execvpe. Kernel sends tty-generated signals to the foreground pgrp only.
in_this_project: minibox/container.py init_main ka CMD branch (os.isatty(0) block). README NOT-done list: 'that code path is written but NOT tested'. PLAN.md Not in scope: TTY allocation (-t).
code_example:
# real, minibox/container.py init_main, CMD branch (trimmed)
            if os.isatty(0):
                # Own process group in the terminal's foreground: Ctrl-C then reaches only the
                # command (as when it runs without minibox), not minibox and INIT as well.
                signal.signal(signal.SIGTTOU, signal.SIG_IGN)
                os.setpgid(0, 0)
                os.tcsetpgrp(0, os.getpgrp())
advantages: Ctrl-C ka behaviour bina minibox jaisa
Sirf terminal case mein chalta hai, pipes par koi effect nahi
disadvantages: Untested code path
Command exit ke baad terminal foreground wapas shell ko dena code nahi karta (shell khud karta hai jab minibox exit hota hai)
Koi pty nahi: container host ke terminal ko seedha use karta hai
common_mistakes: SIGTTOU ignore kiye bina tcsetpgrp call karna (process stop ho jaata)
Ignore ko exec se pehle reset na karna
Sochna ki naye PID namespace se process group / terminal alag ho jaate hain
follow_up_questions: Is path ko automated test kaise karoge (pty.openpty / pexpect jaisa approach)?
docker run -t pty kaise allocate karta hai aur kyun?

question: In the first manual run on the server, `echo $$` inside the container printed 3, not 2. How was this found, what caused it, and what was the fix?
answer_hinglish:
Error identify: design ke mutabik INIT PID 1 aur command PID 2 hona chahiye. Pehle manual run (18:00-18:04) mein echo $$ ne 3 print kiya -- matlab command se pehle namespace mein koi aur process PID 2 le chuka tha.

Likely cause: libc.py pehle ctypes.util.find_library('c') se libc dhoondta tha. find_library Linux par andar ek SUBPROCESS chalata hai (ldconfig -p). libc() lazily load hota hai -- pehli baar tab jab INIT apne naye namespace mein mount() call karta hai. Toh woh ldconfig subprocess naye PID namespace mein PID 2 ban gaya, exit hua, aur phir CMD ko PID 3 mila.

Investigate kaise: PID numbering sequential hai naye namespace mein, toh 'gap' ka matlab ek extra fork. INIT ke setup path mein dekho kaun fork/subprocess karta hai; strace -f -e trace=clone,execve se ldconfig ka execve dikh jaata.

Smallest fix: libc() pehle ctypes.CDLL('libc.so.6', use_errno=True) try karta hai (glibc ka soname, koi subprocess nahi); sirf OSError par find_library fallback. Comment wahi likhta hai: 'inside the container that extra fork would take PID 2 before the user's command does.' Kyun kaam karta hai: dlopen ek library call hai, process nahi banata.

Ab test_command_is_pid_2_and_init_is_pid_1 yeh lock karta hai ($$ == '2'). Lesson: privileged setup path mein hidden forks (subprocess, find_library, shell-outs) namespace state badal dete hain; yeh SERVER_RUN.md section 3 point 1 mein record hai.
why_needed: Hidden subprocesses library calls mein chhupe hote hain; namespace ya cgroup ke andar woh PIDs, pids.max counts aur timing badal dete hain.
real_world_analogy: Queue mein token number 2 aapka hona tha, lekin receptionist ne beech mein apne chai waale ko token 2 de diya (hidden subprocess). Fix: receptionist ko seedha number yaad rakhne do, chai waale ko bulao hi mat.
how_it_works: INIT in new PID ns -> first libc.mount -> libc() -> find_library -> fork+exec ldconfig (PID 2) -> exits -> fork CMD (PID 3). Fix: CDLL('libc.so.6') first -> no fork -> CMD PID 2.
in_this_project: minibox/libc.py libc() function; tests/integration/test_isolation.py::test_command_is_pid_2_and_init_is_pid_1; SERVER_RUN.md 'What went wrong' point 1.
advantages: Fix ek line ka, koi behaviour change nahi
Test ab regression pakadta hai
disadvantages: libc.so.6 glibc-specific hai; musl host par fallback phir subprocess karega
Lazy load ka timing abhi bhi namespace ke andar hai
common_mistakes: PID 3 ko 'cosmetic' samajh kar ignore karna
Bug ko busybox sh ki galti maan lena
find_library ko pure function samajhna
follow_up_questions: libc ko INIT fork hone se pehle host mein eagerly load karna better fix hota kya?
musl-based host par yeh fallback kaise behave karega?
pids.max = 1 ya 2 jaise tight limit mein yeh hidden fork kya karta?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Soname-first loading simple aur fast hai lekin glibc assume karta hai; fallback portability rakhta hai par hidden fork wapas laata hai. Eager loading host mein (fork se pehle) dono problem hal karta par yeh code mein nahi kiya.
advanced.failure_scenarios: musl host par CDLL('libc.so.6') fail -> find_library -> extra PID wapas, aur tight pids.max mein setup fail bhi ho sakta. Koi bhi naya subprocess setup path mein yahi bug laayega -- test PID 2 check karke pakdega.
advanced.alternatives: Fork se pehle host process mein libc() call karke cache karna; os module ke syscalls (3.12 mein mount nahi hai); chhota C extension.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Har container start par ek extra fork+exec hota (ldconfig) -- 100x containers par start time aur load badhta. Fix ke baad yeh cost nahi; start inner 18 ms measured fix ke baad ka hai.
advanced.production_improvements: libc() ko host side par eagerly initialize karna, setup path mein 'no subprocess' assertion (jaise test PID 2), aur musl host par integration run.

question: Walk through minibox/libc.py: how are mount, umount2 and pivot_root called through ctypes, how are errors reported, and what are the portability traps?
answer_hinglish:
Python 3.12 stdlib mein os.unshare, os.fork, os.execvpe, os.chroot, os.mknod, socket.sethostname hain, lekin mount(2), umount2(2), pivot_root(2) nahi. libc.py ~75 lines mein yeh teen wrap karta hai.

1) Lazy load: libc() pehli call par CDLL('libc.so.6', use_errno=True). use_errno=True zaroori hai: ctypes har call ke baad errno ko private copy mein save karta hai, warna Python ka apna code errno overwrite kar deta. Lazy isliye ki module Windows/macOS par import ho (unit tests MS_* constants use karte hain).

2) argtypes: mount ke liye [c_char_p x3, c_ulong, c_char_p], umount2 ke liye [c_char_p, c_int]. Isse flags sahi C type mein jaate hain aur None NULL ban jaata hai. _b() str ko os.fsencode se bytes karta hai, None ko None.

3) _check(ret, what): ret != 0 par ctypes.get_errno() se errno lekar OSError(err, 'mount(...): <strerror>') raise. Yeh OSError run() ke except mein 125 banta hai, aur INIT ke andar 'container setup failed' print.

4) pivot_root: glibc mein wrapper nahi, toh syscall(nr, new_root, put_old). Syscall number architecture-specific hai: SYS_PIVOT_ROOT = {'x86_64': 155, 'aarch64': 41, 'arm64': 41}, platform.machine() se. Unknown arch par saaf OSError. syscall.restype = c_long.

Constants (MS_BIND 4096, MS_REC 16384, MS_PRIVATE 1<<18, MNT_DETACH 2) <sys/mount.h> se, aur test_mount_flag_values_match_linux_headers unhe pin karta hai. Traps: galat syscall number = galat syscall (silent disaster), argtypes na do toh 64-bit flags truncate ho sakte hain, use_errno bhoolo toh errno 0 ya galat.
why_needed: ctypes se syscalls chhota code hai par type aur errno galtiyan silent hoti hain; interview mein FFI boundary ki samajh dikhana important hai.
real_world_analogy: Videsh mein (C libc) baat karne ke liye translator (ctypes): use batana padta hai har shabd ka type kya hai (argtypes), aur jawab ke saath error slip (errno) turant sambhal kar rakhni padti hai, warna agla sawaal use mita deta hai.
how_it_works: Python str -> fsencode bytes -> c_char_p; flags -> c_ulong -> libc.mount -> ret -> _check -> get_errno -> OSError. pivot_root: syscall(c_long(nr), bytes, bytes).
in_this_project: minibox/libc.py: libc, _check, _b, mount, umount2, pivot_root, SYS_PIVOT_ROOT, MS_* constants. Callers: mounts.apply_step (mount), mounts.enter_root (pivot_root, umount2). Unit test tests/unit/test_mounts.py::test_mount_flag_values_match_linux_headers.
advantages: Zero third-party dependencies
Errors errno ke saath readable OSError
Module har OS par import hota hai (lazy load)
disadvantages: Syscall numbers haath se maintain: naye arch par update
argtypes har call par set hote hain (chhota overhead, global CDLL object mutate)
glibc soname assume
common_mistakes: use_errno=True bhool jaana
Flags bina argtypes ke pass karna
pivot_root ke liye galat arch ka syscall number
follow_up_questions: Python 3.12 ke baad os module mein in syscalls ka support aaye toh kya badloge?
Agar 32-bit ARM par chalana ho toh kya check karoge?
ctypes vs cffi vs C extension -- yahan kya choose karte aur kyun?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: ctypes zero-dependency aur har syscall visible rakhta hai (learning goal), lekin type safety aur portability manual hai. Production runtime (runc) Go mein seedha syscall package use karta hai.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Galat syscall number = koi aur syscall chalega (silent). argtypes missing = flags truncate/garbage. Errno save na ho = misleading error. Unknown arch par code saaf OSError deta hai, toh container 125 se fail hota hai bajaye galat call ke.
advanced.alternatives: cffi ya C extension; os.mount jaisa future stdlib API; libmount; Go/C mein runtime likhna (PLAN.md: production choice Go ya C).
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Har mount call per-container chand dafa hota hai; ctypes overhead 18 ms inner start mein included hai. 100x containers par yeh bottleneck nahi lagta (measure nahi kiya).
advanced.production_improvements: argtypes ek baar init par set karna, newer mount API (fsopen/fsmount/move_mount) consider karna, arch table ko test se cross-check karna, aur musl hosts ka support.

question: Coding exercise: implement minibox's CLI so that everything after `--` belongs to the container command (argparse.REMAINDER), and parse sizes like 64M, 1.5G, 64MiB into bytes.
answer_hinglish:
Do pieces hain, dono tests ke saath.

1) Command parsing (cli.build_parser): run subparser mein aakhri positional r.add_argument('command', nargs=argparse.REMAINDER). REMAINDER ka matlab: jahan se positional shuru hua, uske baad ke SAARE args as-is is list mein, chahe woh '--memory' jaise dikhte hon. parse_args() phir agar cmd[0] == '--' hai toh use hata deta hai, aur khaali command par parser.error('run: missing command (put it after --)') -- exit code 2. Test test_command_flags_after_double_dash_are_not_ours: ['--', 'ls', '--memory', '-la'] -> command ['ls', '--memory', '-la'] aur limits default (Limits()). test_command_without_double_dash: '--' optional hai. Bad args (no command, no rootfs, --pids 0, --cpus 0.001, bad hostname, --name ../etc) sab SystemExit 2 (test_bad_arguments_exit_2).

2) Size parsing (cgroups.parse_size, CLI mein _size wrapper jo ValueError ko ArgumentTypeError banata hai): regex '^\s*(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\s*([kKmMgGtT]?)(?:i?[bB])?\s*$'. Units binary (K = 1024), jaise docker --memory. value = float * unit; agar whole number of bytes nahi ('1.3' bytes) toh ValueError; <= 0 bhi reject. Tests: '64M' -> 67108864, '1.5G' -> 3 << 29, '64MiB'/'64MB' -> 64 << 20, ' 2K ' -> 2048; reject '', 'abc', '-1M', '0', '1.3', '10X', 'M'.

CPU validation bhi isi pattern mein: _cpus 0 < v <= 1024 aur round(v * 100000) >= 1000 (kernel ka minimum quota 1 ms per 100 ms).
why_needed: Container CLI mein user ke command ke flags aur runtime ke flags mix na hon -- yeh bug (ls --memory ko minibox ka flag samajhna) bahut common hai.
real_world_analogy: Courier form: '--' ke baad jo likha hai woh parcel ke andar ki chitthi hai, courier company use padhti nahi, as-is deliver karti hai.
how_it_works: argv -> argparse (options until first positional) -> REMAINDER grabs rest -> strip leading '--' -> require non-empty. Size: regex -> number + unit -> float * 1024^k -> integral and > 0 check -> int.
in_this_project: minibox/cli.py build_parser, parse_args, _size, _cpus, _pids, _hostname, _name; minibox/cgroups.py parse_size. Tests tests/unit/test_cli.py aur tests/unit/test_cgroups.py::test_parse_size / test_parse_size_rejects.

Validation fork se pehle, argparse exit 2 ke saath
Size units docker jaise
disadvantages: REMAINDER ke quirks: options ko positional ke baad likho toh woh command mein chale jaate
float se size parse karna bahut bade numbers par precision kho sakta hai
common_mistakes: nargs='*' use karna (tab '--memory' minibox ka flag ban jaata)
'--' ko command ka hissa chhod dena

question: minibox explicitly says it is not a security boundary. If you had to evolve the stage-1 core toward a real runtime, what would you add, in what order, and why?
answer_hinglish:
Pehle honest baseline (README): minibox sab kuch real root ke roop mein chalata hai -- user namespace nahi (container root = host root, test confirm karta hai), capabilities drop nahi (CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_SYS_MODULE, CAP_MKNOD, CAP_SYS_PTRACE sab), seccomp/AppArmor/SELinux nahi, cgroup namespace nahi, /sys nahi par container khud mount kar sakta hai. Toh bina exploit ke escape possible hai: mknod host disk aur mount. pivot_root sirf chroot-style escape band karta hai.

Meri recommended order, impact ke hisaab se:
1) Capability drop + no_new_privs: sabse sasta aur sabse bada effect. CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_MKNOD, CAP_SYS_MODULE hatane se 'mknod + mount host disk' raasta band. Docker ka default capability set jaisa chhota allowlist.
2) Seccomp filter: mount, kexec, module load, keyctl jaise syscalls block -- kernel attack surface kam.
3) User namespace: container ka uid 0 host par unprivileged uid; rootless bhi possible. Yeh sabse invasive hai: uid mapping, rootfs ownership (minibox root ke roop mein image pull karta hai taaki uid 0 owners hon), cgroup delegation sab badlega.
4) /proc masking aur read-only paths (/proc/kcore, /proc/sys), read-only rootfs option.
5) Device cgroup (cgroup v2 mein eBPF) taaki nodes bane bhi toh open na hon.

Har ek ke saath wahi discipline jo chroot escape mein: attack test + control test + mutation. Architecture mein mounts.build_plan jaisa 'data plan' security config ke liye bhi (capabilities list, seccomp profile) -- unit testable. Yeh sab abhi NOT implemented hai.
why_needed: Interviewer dekhna chahta hai ki candidate container isolation aur container security ke fark ko samajhta hai aur priorities justify kar sakta hai.
real_world_analogy: Ghar ki deewarein (namespaces) ban gayi hain, lekin darwaze par taala (caps), CCTV aur rules (seccomp), aur guest ko master key na dena (user ns) abhi baaki hai.
how_it_works: Current: namespaces + pivot_root + cgroups as real root. Target: + capset/bounding set drop + PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS + seccomp BPF + CLONE_NEWUSER with uid/gid maps + masked /proc paths + device controller.
in_this_project: README 'Read this first: it is NOT a security boundary' aur NOT implemented list; PLAN.md 'Not in scope'; test_user_namespace_is_shared_with_the_host jo limitation ko true rakhta hai; container.setup_container jahan in steps ko jodna hoga.
advantages: Clear priority: sabse sasta, sabse bada risk pehle
Har control ke liye testable escape scenario
Existing data-plan pattern reuse
disadvantages: User namespace bahut cheezein badalta hai (ownership, cgroups, overlay in userns)
Seccomp profile maintain karna aur false positives
common_mistakes: Namespaces ko security maan lena
Sirf seccomp lagana aur CAP_SYS_ADMIN chhod dena
Security feature add karna bina escape test ke
follow_up_questions: CAP_SYS_ADMIN kyun 'the new root' kehlata hai?
User namespace ke saath overlayfs aur cgroup delegation mein kya problems aati hain?
Seccomp default-deny vs default-allow profile -- kab kya?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Capabilities + seccomp kam code mein bada fayda dete hain par root-in-container ka fundamental issue nahi hal karte; user namespace woh karta hai lekin sabse invasive hai. Isliye order: cheap high-impact pehle, invasive baad mein.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Aaj: container mknod + mount se host disk padh sakta hai, /sys mount kar sakta hai, modules load kar sakta hai -- sab README mein likha hai. Galat seccomp profile legit programs ko EPERM deta hai; galat uid map par rootfs files ka ownership toot jaata hai.
advanced.alternatives: VM-based isolation (Firecracker/gVisor jaise sandbox) jab hostile code ho; rootless runtimes; LSM profiles (AppArmor/SELinux) capabilities ke saath.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Security controls per-container constant cost hain; 10x-100x containers par seccomp filter ka per-syscall overhead aur uid range allocation (subuid ranges) manage karna padta -- minibox mein measure nahi kiya.
advanced.production_improvements: Default-drop capability set, no_new_privs, default seccomp profile, user namespace with subuid mapping, masked /proc paths, read-only rootfs flag, aur har ek ke liye escape + control tests.

question: How does minibox handle setup failures and cleanup across the three processes (exit 125, the ready pipe, killing INIT, the owned-resources guard), and where are its limits?
answer_hinglish:
Failure handling run() ke try/except/finally mein concentrated hai.

1) Ownership guard: owned = {'cgroup': False, 'state': False}. os.makedirs(state) aur cgroup.create() dono FAIL karte hain agar naam already use mein ho (makedirs bina exist_ok, os.mkdir leaf). Success ke baad hi owned flag True hota hai, aur finally mein cleanup() sirf owned resources ko chhoota hai. Isliye same --name ka doosra container 125 deta hai lekin pehle ka cgroup nahi mitata -- test_two_containers_with_the_same_name_cannot_run_at_once exactly yeh check karta hai.

2) Ready pipe: INIT fork ke baad os.read(ready_r, 1) par rukta hai jab tak host cgroup.add_pid(init_pid) na kar de. Agar add_pid fail ho (OSError), except block INIT ko SIGKILL + waitpid karta hai -- warna woh pipe par hamesha wait karta. Pipe ke bina M13 race: limits+isolation mein 4, 2, 2 failures, aur ek baar fork bomb cgroup ke bahar chala (load avg 3172, systemd session limit ne roka).

3) INIT ke andar: init_main ka koi bhi exception pakda jaata hai, message print, aur os._exit(code) -- kabhi host ke code path mein return nahi (fork ke baad do copies ka khatra). Default 125.

4) cleanup(): cgroup.kill + populated 0 wait, stats, remove; state dir rmtree, lekin agar merged host ns mein mounted dikhe toh RuntimeError bajaye mounted dir delete karne ke. test_failed_setup_also_cleans_up (bad workdir -> 125, state dir aur cgroup gone).

Limits (README honest): minibox khud SIGKILL ho toh koi cleanup nahi -- container chalta rehta hai, cgroup aur state dir bachte hain, koi gc/ps/stop nahi. Shared parent cgroup remove race: doosra container ENOENT se 125. M18 (cgroup.kill skip) pakda nahi gaya kyunki PID 1 exit hone par kernel poora namespace pehle hi maar deta hai.
why_needed: Container runtimes ka sabse mushkil hissa happy path nahi, partial failure ke baad saaf state hai; interview mein yeh ownership aur crash-consistency thinking dikhata hai.
real_world_analogy: Event hall booking: aap sirf woh hall saaf karte ho jo aapne book kiya (owned), doosre ki party ka saaman nahi uthate. Aur agar aapki gaadi hi raste mein toot jaaye (minibox SIGKILL), toh hall gandaa pada rehta hai jab tak koi manager (gc) na aaye.
how_it_works: try: makedirs state (owned) -> build_plan -> cgroup.create (owned) -> pipe -> unshare+fork -> add_pid -> write pipe -> wait. except: kill INIT if started -> 125. finally: reset handlers -> cleanup(owned only).

Tests tests/integration/test_isolation.py::test_failed_setup_also_cleans_up, ::test_two_containers_with_the_same_name_cannot_run_at_once, ::test_state_dir_and_cgroup_are_removed.

cgroup.kill path ka koi test nahi (M18 not caught)

M6 ke time do containers chalte reh gaye aur haath se cgroup.kill karna pada; ab fixture leftovers ko kill karke fail karta hai.
